subject: Culture
title: Mountain Worship
description: A fast breakdown of Mountain Worship for builders.

hook.text: Mount Kailash in Tibet has never been climbed. No government allows it. Four religions consider it sacred.

buildup.text: Mountains are sacred across cultures: Olympus for Greeks, Sinai for Jews, Fuji for Shinto practitioners.

discovery.text: Height creates awe, and awe triggers the brain's 'small self' response—feeling tiny beside something vast.

twist.text: When Edmund Hillary summited Everest in 1953, Sherpas were conflicted. Climbing Chomolungma was touching a goddess.

climax.text: Tourism is desecrating mountains that were protected by reverence. Everest now has a garbage problem.

punchline.text: We stopped worshipping mountains and started trashing them.

quiz.question: How many religions consider Mount Kailash sacred?
